findings.title: Stated corollary 'd3<32 needs d0*d1*d2<=256' contradicts the page rule it is derived from
findings.where: <repo>/docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.md:340-341 (and planning rule 4 at line 383); docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.spec:12-13 (preamble); scripts/state_exec_predict.py:11-12 (docstring)
findings.doc_says: With d3 < 32 a state needs d0*d1*d2 <= 256 (the spec preamble writes it as an implication: d3 < 32 => d0*d1*d2 <= 256). The predictor docstring says 'for d3 < 32 the state must satisfy d0*d1*d2 <= 256'.
findings.reality: The rule the same documents state (padded = rows*64 when d3<32, pass iff ceil(true/16384) == ceil(padded/16384)) predicts PASS for rows > 256 in many cases. Example: 4x128x1x31 gives rows=512, true=31744 B, padded=32768 B, both 2 pages, so PASS. Across d3 in 1..31 and rows in 257..4096 the predictor passes 8,915 pairs. The rule gives a sufficient condition for d3<32, not a necessary one. The rows>256 region is predicted but not asserted by any spec line.
findings.evidence: python3 scripts/state_exec_predict.py 4 128 1 31 -> predicted=PASS rc=0; 4 128 1 16 -> predicted=FAIL rc=1 (padded 32768 vs true 16384, 2 vs 1 pages). Enumeration via importlib (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1) of predict() over d3 1..31, rows 257..4096: 8915 PASS pairs, e.g. (482,17), (483,17).
findings.fix: Restate the corollary as sufficient only ('d3<32 and d0*d1*d2<=256 always executes'), and state that the rows>256 region is predicted by the rule but unmeasured. Either add spec lines for a few such shapes (e.g. 4x128x1x31 PASS, 4x128x1x16 FAIL) or label them tentative. Fix the predictor docstring and spec preamble line 13 to match.

findings.title: live_in definition misses inputs that feed only a (non-returned) state update: they ARE counted
findings.where: docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.md:62-66 (§1 live_in definition) and :376 (§9 rule 1); HANDOFF-2026-10-22.md §3 table row 1
findings.doc_says: "live_in counts declared inputs that are reachable from a returned output. Unreferenced inputs, inputs read only by a dead op, and inputs read only by a dead add-chain are not counted." Combined with §9 rule 1 ("Return a state's update only if you need it"), a reader will treat an input whose only consumer is a state update that is not returned as dead/uncounted.
findings.reality: An input whose only consumer is slice_update -> write_state of a state whose update is NOT returned is counted as live. The write_state side effect is a root of liveness, not only the returned tuple. Unreferenced inputs are still free, so the extra port is attributable to the state-write path. This is exactly the shape of the recommended no-update KV append (new K/V inputs feeding only write_state), so the doc under-counts by one port per such input in the doc's own recommended configuration.

findings.title: An input returned directly as an output is not counted at execution (law is not 'iff'), yields all-zero data, and is counted at the frontend
findings.where: docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.md:57-68 (§1 law, 'unique_out counts distinct returned tensors') and §9 rule 1; HANDOFF §3 row 1
findings.doc_says: "A program executes on the ANE iff live_in + unique_out (+ ...) <= 127"; unique_out = distinct returned tensors. Nothing says a returned input is special.

The frontend (validate) still counts the returned input. identity/reshape/relu/sigmoid outputs of an input count as normal outputs; only the bare `return x_i` is exempt.

findings.title: Unreferenced state<> params are free at execution (but counted at the frontend), contradicting 'every state<> param counts as one input port'
findings.where: docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.md:126-128 (§3 law), :376 (§9 rule 1, n_states); §3 'Not measured' sentence
findings.doc_says: "In both caps, every state<> param counts as one input port"; rule 1 uses n_states.
findings.reality: At execution a declared-but-never-referenced state is pruned like a dead input and costs no port; at validate/compile it is counted. Only referenced states (read-update-write, used read-only) cost a port. Over-counting is conservative, but the stated law is false for this case. States whose read is dead (no write) or that are write-only do not even compile on the run path, so no 'dead read still costs a port' point exists to check.

Dead-read state (read_state result unused, no write_state): `E5RT encountered an STL exception. msg = State Operation dependencies are violated after program modification` (san_ro_dead); write-only state: `ANECCompile() FAILED` (san_wo).
findings.fix: Qualify §3 and §9: n_states counts states reachable from the program roots at execution; all declared states at validate/compile. Optionally note dead-read and write-only states are not constructible.

findings.title: Zero-output claim in §2 is wrong in both halves
findings.where: docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.md:118-119 (§2); no spec line asserts it (the doc's own rule says such a sentence is a hypothesis)
findings.doc_says: "Zero-output programs are rejected by validate (CompilationFailure). compile still emits an artifact, but it does not load or run."
findings.reality: It splits on whether the program has states. Stateless zero-output (`-> ()`): validate AND compile both fail with CompilationFailure (compile leaves only a 0-byte additional_weights.bin, no macho), run fails with `produced an empty program!`. Zero-plain-output program WITH states (noupd): validate ACCEPTS (rc=0), compile emits a 32-64 KiB macho (rc=0), run fails. The artifact-emitting case is the stateful one, which the BAR section relies on.

findings.title: d3<32 necessity corollary is wrong; the page rule it sits under is an iff
findings.where: md L340-341 (also spec L13 header, scripts/state_exec_predict.py L11-12 docstring)
findings.doc_says: With d3 < 32, a state needs d0*d1*d2 <= 256. Section 9 rule 4 repeats the limit.
findings.reality: The rule in the same section (L333-337) is an iff: PASS iff ceil(true/16384) == ceil(padded/16384). It predicts PASS for (1,300,1,31) (rows 300; true 18600 B and padded 19200 B, both 2 pages) and for (4,128,1,17) (rows 512; 2 pages on both sides). Runner copy-records state-exec-pages reports [1,300,1,31] PASS on hardware, with narrow escapes noted. A compiler following the corollary would reject valid states. The rule is correct; the corollary is not.
findings.evidence: Predictor computed in memory from the md rule: (1,300,1,31) gives pages_true=2 pages_padded=2 PASS; (4,128,1,17) gives 2 and 2 PASS; (1,260,1,31) gives 1 and 2 FAIL. Runner JSON copy-records state-exec-pages statement and measurement. No spec line tests either case.

findings.title: fp16-only state dtype law is wrong: int8, uint8, int16 and bool states compile and execute
findings.where: ane-port-limits-h17.md:346-348 (dtype 'established'), :383 (rule 4 'Use fp16 only'), :420-423 (open question 5); HANDOFF-2026-10-22.md:71; scripts/gen_states_nd.py:19
findings.doc_says: 'Only fp16 states compile on this path. fp32 fails with CompilationFailure; int8/uint8/int16/int32/bool fail with InvalidMILProgram.' Label: established. Open Q5 adds that the dim1=16 special case cannot be resolved 'since only fp16 compiles'. The spec has no line for any of this.
findings.reality: Only fp32 and int32 STATES are rejected. int8, uint8, int16 and bool states compile and run on the ANE. The original probe changed the dtype of the whole program (state, plain io and the add op). The InvalidMILProgram failures come from add/io in those dtypes. A stateless 'y = add(x,x)' in int32/int8/bool is rejected identically, and a stateless fp32 add gives CompilationFailure. Keeping io and compute fp16 and changing only the state dtype gives rc=0 and 'step 0:' for int8, uint8, int16 and bool, twice each. The raw state bytes show the dtype is real: an int8 state written with ones reads back through milc's fp16 dump as 0x0101 (1.53e-05, 2 of 16 'nonzero'), and an int16 state as 0x0001 (5.96e-08, 4 of 16). Consequences: (a) the writeup would steer a compiler away from int8/uint8/int16 KV caches; (b) Open Q5 is resolvable, and the answer is ELEMENTS: for int8, int16, bool and fp16 alike the tag is 0x9360/0x9364 exactly at dim1=16 and the stride word and rowbits depend on dim1 as an element count (16 B int8 rows behave like 32 B fp16 rows), so the '16 elements' reading holds and 'log2 of row bytes' does not; (c) the page rule is dtype-dependent: int16 matches the fp16 rule 30/30, but 1-byte dtypes do not follow it (26 of 40 int8 shapes disagreed with a byte-scaled rule). A candidate rule fits 108 of 108 int8, uint8 and bool points (60 random int8 plus 48 targeted across the three dtypes): the buffer is sized as 2 B x elements, rows are laid out at 64 B granularity with 1 B elements, and the state runs iff padded_pages <= true_pages. Only about 2 of the 60 random int8 shapes were failures, so this is a weak fit and should be treated as a hypothesis.

findings.title: Page-rule corollary 'd3 < 32 => d0*d1*d2 <= 256' is false for d3 = 17..31, and the doc contradicts its own predictor
findings.doc_says: 'With d3 < 32, a state needs d0*d1*d2 <= 256' and the table's 'd3 < 32 => d0*d1*d2 <= 256'. Rule 4 says 'keep d3 % 32 == 0, or d0*d1*d2 <= 256'.
findings.reality: The rule itself (equal 16 KiB page counts) is correct and the corollary is not. rows <= 256 is sufficient for every d3 < 32, but necessary only for d3 <= 16. For d3 = 17..31 states with rows > 256 execute when the padding does not cross a page boundary. Hardware, twice each: [5,53,1,31] rows=265 PASS while [8,33,1,31] rows=264 FAIL; [2,241,1,17] rows=482 PASS while [13,37,1,17] rows=481 FAIL; [2,171,1,24] rows=342 PASS while [11,31,1,24] rows=341 FAIL; the assigned [1,300,1,31] PASS while [1,260,1,31] FAIL. state_exec_predict.py predicts each of these correctly. Exhaustive enumeration gives rows > 256 passing for every d3 in 17..31 (first rows: 482, 456, 432, 410, 391, 373, 357, 342, 328, 316, 304, 293, 283, 274, 265) and none for d3 <= 16. The 'needs' wording is a necessity claim and it is false. The error is in the conservative direction, so it costs capacity rather than correctness.
findings.evidence: WD/out_page.txt and out_page2.txt (rows above, with predictor output in predictions_page.txt). Enumeration: Python loop over state_exec_predict.predict for d3 in 1..31 and rows 257..4096.
findings.fix: State the rule as 'ceil(true/16384) == ceil(padded/16384)' only, and call it an equivalence. Give the corollary as: d3 <= 16 => rows <= 256 is necessary and sufficient; 17 <= d3 <= 31 => rows <= 256 is sufficient but not necessary. Point planners at state_exec_predict.py. Correct the same sentence in the HANDOFF table and the predictor header.

findings.title: 'Row width and region' paragraph omits the dim3 = 1 qualifier, and the stride/rowbits laws change for KV-like shapes
findings.where: ane-port-limits-h17.md:311-318 (rowbits = 16*dim1, region = dim1 MiB), :299-309 (stride), :308-309 ('dim2 > 1 adds bits')
findings.doc_says: 'rowbits = 16*dim1 (row width in fp16 bits, mod 2^16), and region = rowbits << 16 = dim1 MiB.' Stride is scoped to dim2 = dim3 = 1, but the rowbits/region sentence carries no scope, and only dim2 > 1 is said to add stride bits.
findings.reality: rowbits = 16*dim1 holds only for dim3 <= 8. For dim1=4: d3=16 gives rowbits 128, d3=17 gives 192, d3=31/32 gives 256, d3=64 gives 512, d3=128 gives 1024, d3=200 gives 1600, d3>=256 saturates at 2048. That fits 16*dim1*ceil(d3/8) below saturation. region is therefore not dim1 MiB (e.g. [4,4,1,31] region=16777216, [4,8,1,128] region=134217728). The stride word also picks up 2^19 once d3 >= 129: [4,4,1,128] stride 16, [4,4,1,129] stride 524304 (0x80010), [4,8,1,200] stride 524312; dim2 > 1 adds small increments (dim1=8: d2=2,3 give 26; d2=4,5 give 27; d2=8,16 give 28). Realistic KV shapes are therefore outside §6's rowbits/region/stride laws: [4,16,1,128] stride 32 rowbits 4096, [4,16,4,64] stride 33, [1,32,2048,128] stride 32 rowbits 8192. Separately, 'dim1 MiB' wraps: dim1=4096 and 8192 decode to region=0, dim1=5000 to 947912704 (the doc says 'mod 2^16' for rowbits but not for the region identity). The decoder's rowbits triple is internally consistent (rowbits_ok True) in all these cases, so these are real record contents, not decode noise.
findings.evidence: WD/out_d3.txt, out_d3thr.txt, out_kv.txt, out_stride2.txt. Python check of decode()['rowbits_ok'] on d3_31..d3_512 and kv_* machos: all True.
findings.fix: Scope the rowbits/region/stride sentences with '(dim2 = dim3 = 1)'. Add the observed d3 sub-laws as tentative (rowbits = 16*dim1*ceil(d3/8) for d3 up to 255, saturating at 2048 for dim1=4; stride += 2^19 for d3 >= 129). Add that region = dim1 MiB only for dim1 < 4096. Add one spec line with a d3 > 1 shape.

findings.title: Binding-record format law ('established') fails in three ordinary regimes; decode_slot_ordinals reports format_ok=0 on the doc's own 54-state program
findings.doc_says: Every 0x9344/0x934a/0x9442 record is [tag][bar_word][offset][0] with bar_word = 0x2300 + 0x80*ordinal of an __FVMLIB segment ('established, h17 and h16g', no domain given), and decode_slot_ordinals.py 'validates every record against the segment table'.
findings.reality: Three regimes emit records whose bar_word is below 0x2300, so ordinal < 0 and the shipped decoder prints format_ok=0: (a) NO PLAIN INPUT (fill update source): exactly one 0x9344 record has bar_word 0x2080 (ordinal -5). All 52 no-input artifacts tested (h17 and h16g) give format_ok=0, including the 54-state program the doc uses for its headline claim. In this regime raw 0x9344 count is K+2 (decoder-valid K+1), so the formula K+max(1,min(in,out)) gives K+1 and is off by one on the raw count. (b) ANY NON-UNIFORM PER-CHANNEL INLINE CONSTANT operand (mul/add by const[1,C,1,1] with distinct values, even C=4): two 0x934a records with bar_word 0x2080, format_ok=0 (uniform consts are folded into an immediate and stay format_ok=1). (c) Intermediates larger than ~2 MiB spill to a __DATA.__bss scratch segment: dozens of 0x9344/0x9442 records with bar_word 0x2180 (ordinal -3), format_ok=0. So the 'ordinal = BAR id' reading covers only the FVMLIB-resident buffers; real models (biases/scales, big activations) will hit (b) and (c) routinely. The 0x2080/0x2180 words look like additional non-FVMLIB BAR/address classes (0x41 = constant/fill source, 0x43 = DATA scratch; meaning inferred, not established). The BAR-pool cap numbers are NOT affected.

findings.title: '0x9442 = #__data sections' and 'never more than 57 segments' are false once an intermediate exceeds ~2 MiB (DATA scratch segment)
findings.doc_says: '#0x9442 = #__data sections' (Section economy, established); 'one destination binding per __data section'; the Mach-O 'never has more than 57 LC_SEGMENT_64 ... across 1,284 artifacts, 0 violations'.
findings.reality: When an intermediate tensor is larger than roughly 2 MiB (sz=100 -> 2.0 MB no scratch; sz=104 -> 2.25 MB scratch, even a single op), the compiler adds a '__DATA 0x800000 [__bss]' segment as segment 1 and each spilled intermediate adds a 0x9442 (and 0x9344) record bound to it. Then 0x9442 = data_sections + (#spilled intermediates) (e.g. +30 for a 30-op chain) and the Mach-O has 58 segments (fvmlib=55 + PAGEZERO + TEXT + __DATA). The scratch segment does NOT consume a BAR id from the 55-pool: with it present N=53 + plain input compiles and runs, N=54 fails; and N=54 with no plain input compiles (58 segments) while N=55 fails. So the 53/54 numbers stand, but the section-economy law and the segment-count invariant do not hold for realistic activation sizes.

findings.title: Kernel-segment mechanism is wrong: shedding __KERN_0 and packing are independent decisions; the segment is kept whenever a BAR id is free
findings.where: docs/spec/ane-port-limits-h17.md:179-188 (contrast scripts/hwx_layout.py:10 which says 'shed when the budget needs the slot')
findings.doc_says: Split layout includes __KERN_0 if the program has a LUT op; 'Otherwise the compiler sheds __KERN_0 (folding the table into __TEXT), packs every non-surface __data ... one segment'.
findings.reality: Layout choice depends only on B (const+data sections): B<=55 -> split, else packed (fvmlib prediction confirmed). Separately __KERN_0 is kept iff total ids <= 55: B+1<=55 -> split + kern; B==55 -> split with kern SHED (not packed); B>=56 -> packed, kern RETAINED if packed+1<=55 (shed only at the edge, e.g. N=53 with a plain input). __KERN_0 is also produced by conv (no LUT) and there is always exactly one regardless of how many LUT ops. Does not change the N cap; matters for anyone counting BAR ids or segments per program.
